title: Claude Fable 5 Made Permanent by Anthropic
description: Simon Willison analyzes Anthropic's decision to make Claude Fable 5 permanent in Max and Team Premium plans at 50% limits, reversing previous plan to remove subscriber access. Competition from GPT-5.6 Sol made Anthropic's original plan untenable. Discusses implications for compute capacity and pricing strategies.
author: Simon Willison

title: Replit Engineers Triple Code Output with AI
description: Amjad Masad reports that Replit engineers have 'nearly tripled code output' in the past six months due to AI completely changing how they work. Demonstrates massive productivity gains from AI coding tools in real production environment.
author: Amjad Masad

title: Firefox Compiled to WebAssembly Runs in Browser
description: Simon explores Puter's achievement of compiling Firefox to WebAssembly so it runs entirely in another browser. Project used estimated $25,000 worth of Claude Opus and Fable tokens but cost less with Claude Max subscription. Discusses technical implementation, WebSocket proxying, and end-to-end encryption.
author: Simon Willison

title: Kimi K3 and the Pelican Benchmark Analysis
description: Comprehensive analysis of Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 model (2.8T parameters), comparing it against the pelican benchmark. Discusses the model's capabilities, promised open weights release by July 27, 2026, and competitive positioning in the LLM landscape.
author: Simon Willison

title: Inkling Open Weights Model Released by Thinking Machines Lab
description: Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling, an Apache-2.0 licensed Mixture-of-Experts transformer with 975B total parameters (41B active). Model is positioned as strong base for fine-tuning rather than frontier model. Simon tests image generation capabilities with pelican prompt.
author: Simon Willison

title: I've Never Felt This Behind - Karpathy on AI Coding in 2026
description: Andrej Karpathy discusses feeling 'never more behind as a programmer' despite coining 'vibe coding' last year. He attended Sequoia AI Ascent 2026 and is using LLMs to build personal knowledge systems. The discussion covers how AI is rapidly transforming programming workflows.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: xAI Grok Build Open Source After Privacy Backlash
description: xAI open sourced Grok Build codebase (844,530 lines of Rust) after severe community backlash over feature that uploaded entire directories to cloud. Simon analyzes the codebase, compares with OpenAI Codex, and explores tool implementations and privacy protections.
author: Simon Willison

title: Claude WebFetch Data Exfiltration Vulnerability
description: Security analysis of Ayush Paul's discovery of data exfiltration vulnerability in Claude's web_fetch tool. The attack used nested generated links to extract private user data. Simon explains the protection mechanism, the loophole found, and Anthropic's fix removing ability to navigate to links within fetched content.
author: Simon Willison

title: 2026 Will Be the 'Slopacolypse' - Karpathy Prediction
description: Discussion about Karpathy's prediction that 2026 will be the 'Slopacolypse' where AI is suddenly writing most code. Quote: 'I am starting to atrophy my ability to write...' reflecting concerns about skill atrophy in AI-assisted coding era.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: DOOMQL: SQLite as Game Engine
description: Peter Gostev's DOOMQL built using GPT-5.6 Sol - a Doom-like game where SQL owns movement, collision, enemies, combat and every pixel. Simon runs the game, explores the SQLite database, and builds a Datasette App with real-time game viewer and tactical map using AI assistance.
author: Simon Willison

title: Datasette Code Frequency Chart Shows AI Impact
description: Simon analyzes GitHub code frequency chart for Datasette project, showing major spike in activity aligning with Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol. Provides quantitative illustration of coding agents' impact on development output.
author: Simon Willison

title: Directly Responsible Individuals (DRI) and AI Agents
description: Simon explores the concept of DRI from Apple/GitLab in context of LLM-powered agents. Argues agents should never be considered DRI for projects as accountability is uniquely human. References IBM's 1979 principle that computers must never make management decisions.
author: Simon Willison
